actions.reason: RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary now splits text through a new _split_text method. When the tokenizer uses the default GPT-4 split pattern, compiled unchanged, _split_text runs an equivalent pattern with the standard library re module, which is cheaper than the regex module on the same input. The stdlib pattern writes letters as [^\W\d_], numbers as \d, whitespace as \s and the remaining classes as [^\s\w]|_. The possessive quantifiers are dropped because backtracking cannot change any match in those alternatives. The fast path only runs when every distinct character of the text gets the same class (letter, number, whitespace, other) from both modules. That is checked by running one findall from each module on the string of distinct characters. It also requires that the text has no characters that case-fold onto the contraction letters (U+017F, U+212A). Otherwise it falls back to regex.findall exactly as before. Outputs are identical in the equivalence harness. encode_ir ratio was 0.9844, and the other metrics stayed within their guards.

journal.text:
I changed RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary in minbpe/regex.py to split text through a new _split_text method. When the tokenizer uses the default GPT-4 split pattern compiled unchanged, _split_text runs an equivalent pattern with the stdlib re module instead of the regex module. Letters become [^\W\d_], numbers \d, whitespace \s.

The first evaluation was rejected. The candidate build failed and the test_encode_decode_identity cases failed for all three tokenizers. After further edits around line 456, evaluation 3 was accepted with identical outputs. encode_ir went from 629260542 to 619415634, ratio 0.9844. The other metrics rose slightly: train_basic_ir 1.0033, train_regex_ir 1.0025, decode_ir 1.0014, save_load_ir 1.0015. The candidate is submitted with 23 changed lines and is queued for replay.

The split step is a real share of encode cost, and stdlib re handles the default pattern more cheaply. The gain is small.

Next, look at the merge loop in encode_chunk, and check why the untouched metrics moved up at all.
